transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I just can’t sit still in these meetings or trainings anymore—I feel like I’ve got to get up and move even when everyone else is fine staying put. It's really starting to cause some trouble for me at work.

Have you ever had a period lasting several days when you felt unusually energetic or euphoric, needed much less sleep, and were more talkative or impulsive than usual? Or has this restlessness been more constant over time?

No, I've never had phases like that where I'm suddenly euphoric or don't need sleep; it's always been a constant, daily thing for me. My kids joke that I'm like a wind-up toy every single day, and my teachers were complaining about me not staying in my seat all the way back in grade school.

Besides being unable to stay seated, did you also have trouble paying attention or acting impulsively as a child, and does that still happen in more than one setting now, like at home as well as at work?

Yes, my mom always got calls from my grade school teachers because I'd wander around and blurt out answers instead of sitting quietly. It absolutely happens at home too—my wife gets frustrated because I can't sit still during church or bingo, and even on my days off I'm constantly pacing and doing chores instead of just relaxing on the couch.

This supports a childhood-onset hyperactivity/impulsivity syndrome rather than an episodic mood condition; the patient specifically denies distinct periods of euphoric mood, decreased need for sleep, or other episodic changes that would suggest an alternative explanation.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports a persistent pattern of hyperactivity/impulsivity beginning in childhood and continuing into adulthood across multiple settings, with associated work impairment. Symptoms are chronic rather than episodic, arguing against mood-related causes such as mania.
